0201Decision.asmediaRecommendation: 0201 for USB4 coupling capacitors and discharge resistors; PCIe page 5 permits 0402 coupling capacitors.
0201Decision.usbIfSupport: 2019 USB4 system presentation, slide 49: smaller components improve return loss; this is design guidance, not universal proof that every 0402 implementation fails.
0201Decision.decision: Retain in this revision. A larger footprint is a channel redesign requiring parasitic/layout verification, not a like-for-like substitution.

handAssemblyDecision.limits: New resistor/0402 shopping costs and minimum quantities not quoted. Accessibility, soldering time and rework risk remain. Hand assembly of existing geometry does not require enlarging footprints.

resistorConsolidationCandidates.change: Use the same 0.1% 12.1 kohm selection for the existing 1% R_RST_N and the buck divider bottoms.
resistorConsolidationCandidates.status: BOM candidate only; verify footprint, ratings and current price/stock.

resistorConsolidationCandidates.change: Use a single appropriate 0.1% 10 kohm type for the existing ordinary 10 kohm roles and the precision supervisor divider bottom.
resistorConsolidationCandidates.status: May increase unit cost; retain ratings and required divider tolerance.

conditionalCurrentManufacturingRequireme: Keep ENIG for the current 0.20-0.25 mm BGA lands unless JLC explicitly approves OSP for the exact construction.
Retain 0.15/0.25 mm vias and fill/cap for current exports; price settings cannot replace a fanout redesign.
Filled/capped via covering is USD 0 in the quoted six-layer job; deleting it has no quoted saving.
Standard assembly is required by the current 0.46 mm bridge pitch and 0201 parts; replacing passives alone does not unlock Economic.
findingsNotClosedByCostAudit: Bridge reset on short power interruptions
conclusion: USD 406.07 is consistent with this specific JLCPCB prototype configuration and its published assembly fee model. It is not evidence of an optimized design or the lowest market quote. The best large cost-reduction candidate is a validated cheaper stackup/power construction, not replacing the USB4 0201 network. No verified two-board USD 200 delivered design was established.
